question: Gorgonia ventalina is the scientific name of which saltwater invertebrate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Common sea fan**__ .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Common sea fan**

 
 
• **Gorgonia ventalina** is the scientific name for the **Common sea fan**, a species of soft coral found in saltwater environments.
 
• It belongs to the phylum **Cnidaria** and the family **Gorgoniidae**.
 
• Common sea fans are characterized by their fan-like shape and vibrant colors, often found in shallow tropical and subtropical waters.
 
• They are filter feeders, relying on plankton and organic matter for nutrition.
 
• Gorgonia ventalina plays a vital role in marine ecosystems by providing habitat and shelter for various marine organisms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sea cucumber:**

 
 
• Sea cucumbers belong to the class **Holothuroidea** and are echinoderms, not related to Gorgonia ventalina.
 
• They have elongated, soft bodies and are found on the ocean floor, often in deep-sea environments.
 
• Sea cucumbers are known for their role in recycling nutrients and maintaining marine ecosystem health.
 
• They are not corals and do not have a fan-like structure like Gorgonia ventalina.
 
• Examples include species like **Holothuria scabra** and **Apostichopus japonicus**.
 
 
 
• **Sea urchin:**
 
 
• Sea urchins belong to the class **Echinoidea** and are also echinoderms, unrelated to Gorgonia ventalina.
 
• They have a spherical or flattened body covered with spines and are found in oceans worldwide.
 
• Sea urchins are herbivores, feeding on algae and playing a crucial role in controlling algal growth in marine ecosystems.
 
• They are not corals and lack the fan-like structure of Gorgonia ventalina.
 
• Examples include species like **Strongylocentrotus purpuratus** and **Diadema antillarum**.
 
 
 
• **Sea anemone:**
 
 
• Sea anemones belong to the class **Anthozoa** and are related to corals but are not the same as Gorgonia ventalina.
 
• They are solitary polyps with tentacles surrounding a central mouth, often found attached to rocks or coral reefs.
 
• Sea anemones are predators, using their tentacles to capture small fish and plankton.
